questions.q: Who was entrusted with looking after the Prophet SAW after Abdul Muttalib died?
questions.explain: All of Makkah grieved when Abdul Muttalib died, and the Prophet was entrusted to Abu Talib.

questions.q: What was Abu Talib's family situation?
questions.explain: Abu Talib was poor with five children, but loved the Prophet SAW even more than his own.

questions.q: What happened to the small amount of food when the Prophet SAW ate with them?
options: It ran out before everyone ate
questions.explain: That is barakah: a little becomes enough for many.

questions.q: At what age did the Prophet SAW start tending sheep?
questions.explain: At eight or nine he tended sheep for the people of Makkah for a few cents.

questions.q: What did he learn in the desert while tending sheep?
options: To be brave facing wolves and the night, and to live simply
questions.explain: In the desert he learnt to be brave and to live with little.

questions.q: What lesson is there in the Prophet SAW working as a shepherd from a young age?
options: Work is nothing to be ashamed of
questions.explain: Every prophet tended sheep. Work is no shame even when the pay is small.

questions.q: Where did the Prophet SAW beg to go with Abu Talib at almost 12 years old?
questions.explain: He begged to be taken to Sham with Abu Talib.

questions.q: Abdul Muttalib would not eat without his grandson.
questions.explain: True. He also hugged his grandson tightly when he came back. It is an example of a grandfather's love.

questions.q: Every prophet worked as a shepherd.
questions.explain: True. The Prophet SAW said that no prophet was sent except that he had tended sheep.

questions.q: The Prophet SAW grabbed food and raised his voice when eating.
questions.explain: False. He did not grab, did not raise his voice and waited for others to take first.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: He begs to go to Sham
He looks for his grandfather's camel

questions.explain: He looked for his grandfather's camel, his grandfather died, there was barakah in Abu Talib's house, then he tended sheep, and finally he wanted to go to Sham.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: A person who looks after and guides sheep
A child who lost both mother and father
Likes to help and feed people in need

questions.explain: An orphan has lost both parents, a generous person likes to help, a cousin is the child of an uncle, and a shepherd looks after sheep.
